answers.answer: No. Under 29 U.S.C. 49a(7), except in section 49l–2 of this title, "State agency", used without further description, means an agency designated or authorized under section 49c of this title. Under section 49c, the Governor designates or authorizes the creation of the State agency in accordance with a State statute accepting the provisions of the chapter, and the agency must be vested with all powers necessary to cooperate with the Secretary under the chapter.

No. Under the definition in 29 U.S.C. 49a(6), an "employment service office" means a local office of a State agency. The statute does not require the local office itself to accept appropriations or exercise designation authority; rather, pursuant to section 49c, the State accepts chapter provisions by State statute to obtain apportioned appropriations, and the Governor designates or authorizes the creation of the State agency.
No. The definition of "State agency" in 29 U.S.C. 49a(7) expressly contains the exception "except in section 49l–2 of this title" and therefore cannot be applied without that stated exception.
